sources.quote: Roger Penrose got half of the 2020 Physics Nobel Prize 'for the discovery that black hole formation is a robust prediction of the general theory of relativity'.

Since Penrose started in algebraic geometry as a PhD student of Hodge in Cambridge, he was undoubtedly influenced by the theory of Riemann surfaces in finding this concept (like Weyl, as mentioned in the historical introduction).
This prize was well deserved, since, jointly with Hawking and others, Penrose has shaped our (mathematical) thinking about general relativity ( gr) and black holes since the 1960s–1970s.
To overcome this, Penrose launched his cosmic censorship conjecture(s), whose evolution we discuss.
His 1965 singularity theorem (for which he got the prize) does not in fact imply the existence of black holes (even if its assumptions are met).
The analysis of such space–times is greatly facilitated by Penrose's conformal diagrams, now called Penrose diagrams.
1 Department of Mathematics, Radboud University, Nijmegen, The Netherlands
